fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

## Event and scope

Fix-It Saturday is scheduled for October 17, from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The work area is the library parking court. The meeting room is the rain alternative, and the library remains open to regular visitors during the event. Account for both the public entrance and the book-drop lane.

There are 45 people on the RSVP list, but they may not all arrive, and the number of walk-ins is unknown. Do not treat the RSVP total as a promise that all 45 people will be present at once. The event has eight repair volunteers and three welcome and food volunteers. No volunteer names, repair skill lists, or availability beyond event day have been provided.

The event is for small household-item and clothing repairs. Guests may bring lamps, small appliances, toys, or garments. The team is not accepting gas appliances, microwaves, or items requiring welding. Devices must be unplugged before reaching a repair table. A volunteer may decline an item if it is unsafe, outside their skills, or likely to take longer than the event allows. Explain how intake and a respectful decline could work. Do not promise that every item can be fixed; distinguish a repair attempt from a completed repair.

## Coordinator messages and resources

Nora, the site coordinator, sent this message: “We can use the east gate from 8:15, but please keep the book-drop lane clear.” Nora can open the meeting room if rain makes the outdoor setup unsuitable. The room holds at most 32 people at a time, including volunteers; this is not a 32-person cap for the entire day. The current rain idea is to move the welcome and repair stations indoors, limit entry when the room is full, and ask arriving guests to wait outside until space opens. No separate covered waiting area is listed, so do not assume one is available. The event hours remain 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. if the room is used.

Dev, who is handling facilities, sent this message: “I have six folding tables, eighteen chairs, two extension cords, and the blue tape. Please tell me by Thursday if the room layout needs the tables.” These are the available quantities, not an allocation to particular stations. Blue tape may mark the walk-in route and a clear lane, but it has not been confirmed that there is enough tape for every proposed marking. The two extension cords are the only cords listed. Do not add power strips, extra tables, or tools to the inventory. If a proposed layout depends on an unlisted item, identify it as something to check, not as something already provided.

Marta, who is organizing refreshments, said: “I can bring tea, coffee, apples, and individually wrapped oat bars; I still need to check the allergy labels.” The three welcome and food volunteers have no assigned names or shifts. Treat the label check as unfinished; do not describe any food as allergen-free or add a meal, bottled water, or other refreshments as confirmed. Suggest a workable welcome and refreshment arrangement using the listed items, and make clear what still needs checking.

## Requested plan

1. Provide an event-day sequence that covers setup, guest opening, repair intake, breaks if practical, last intake, and cleanup. Setup may begin at 8:15 at the east gate. Do not move guest opening earlier than 9:30 a.m. or extend closing past 3:30 p.m. Leave exact volunteer assignments open because none have been made.
2. Suggest an arrival and intake process, including a simple way to match each guest's item with an available volunteer. Do not imply that expertise in electrical work, sewing, or any other repair category has been confirmed. Include the stated repair limits, the unplugged-device requirement, and a respectful way to decline unsuitable work.
3. Suggest a use of the six tables and eighteen chairs that stays within the listed quantities, and explain how the book-drop lane can remain clear. Include the rain alternative, the meeting room's limit of 32 people at one time including volunteers, and the stated approach of limiting entry and asking guests to wait outside when the room is full. Do not assume a covered waiting area.
4. Account for the uncertain number of walk-ins, the RSVP list, and the unfinished allergy-label check. Keep these as planning considerations, not claims that a queue or a particular number of arrivals is certain. Flag unresolved details for the coordinators to check rather than deciding them.

The event will not collect repair fees. Keep the plan useful to the coordinators, with concrete actions tied to the supplied notes rather than invented supplies, staffing, or decisions. Use a numbered section for the event-day sequence. Carry all the source notes and coordinator quotes forward, and provide the prompt only—not the completed event plan. Do not send or address anything to Ellis."}]
